doc_friction.issue: Item 1 still makes every run check the perf backlog, which has had no workable item since 2026-11-26 (P063, P064 and P086 are owner rows). The check costs only one command, but the prompt itself says thirty-odd runs reported it for nothing.

A 1,000-run reading takes about 4 minutes and prints only per-workflow medians. To find which workflows lack sparse-checkout I had to grep the workflow files by hand. A column flagging full checkouts would save that step.

deviations.why: I wrote no post in docs/posts/. A 1% CI pool saving with an index-backed sparse checkout is agent-facing knowledge, and the history doc covers it. There is no reader-facing finding.
deviations.result: The next perf run has a ranked list.

deviations.why: I timed ai-bookkeeper's suite first. It is flat (351 files, max 3.4 s), so the pool reading's largest unowned checkout went first. real-estate-agent-photo-app, a for-profit product's CI, came second.
deviations.result: About 18 job-minutes an hour saved at the window's rate.

notes: Metric: CI checkout seconds per job. agent-permission-harness CI went from 44 s median checkout and 72 s median job (ci_profile.py --runs 1000, 2026-11-27 01:55-02:57 UTC, n=22) to 8 s checkout and 34 s job (PR run 45931968964, step timestamps). real-estate-agent-photo-app CI went from 38 s median checkout and 65 s job (n=8) to 1-2 s checkout per job (run 45931969023). Same answers: harness.py --json and the markdown report are cmp-identical between the full tree and a 14,321-file sparse worktree. Without the patch the sparse tree gives 12,088 files instead of 56,021. CI's log reports 56021. 94 unit tests pass in both trees, plus the new TestSparseCheckout, which fails without the patch. sparse_checkout_verify.py on real-estate: all 10 steps match, exit 0. Estimated saving: about 18 job-min an hour, roughly 1% of the pool.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), fetched 2026-11-12. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads are 0.1x input except 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1 and 5.2. Sonnet 5.5 cache_read was 0.20 here until 2026-11-12 (quality audit round 48): records priced before then overstate Sonnet 5.5 cost.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer profiling CI, patching the probe and verifying both trees

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
